text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Industry Minister Franck Borotra says government does not want to help finance restructuring plan presented by French carmakers including 40,000 early retirements. Renault is expected to present a heavy job cutting plan.
-- Elf Aquitaine oil group posts a seven-billion-franc profit for 1996.
-- ABN Amro-France considers boosting its investment bank activity.

-- State to guarantee insurer GAN's activity for up to 20 billion francs, as part of a restructuring plan involving an immediate recapitalisation limited to some four billion francs to avoid having too wide an impact on the 1997 French budget.
-- Bouygues chairman Martin Bouygues and TF1 chairman Patrick Le Lay held in custody over alleged fake billing in construction contracts.
-- Analysts confident in activity outlook of supermarkets group Carrefour.
-- Casino supermarkets chain chairman Georges Plassat does not rule out an alliance with a competitor.
-- Disney Channel to be launched in France via Canal Plus channel CanalSatellite and cable television.
-- Higher oil prices and improved refining activity boost Elf Aquitaine's 1996 profits.
